purpose: Defines ordinary public applicability traits referenced by Adaptive Research nodes. Traits describe biological/civilizational capabilities or constraints; they are not playable-race IDs. Biochemical traits are composable: solvent, backbone/substrate, temperature regime, and structural strategy are separate dimensions rather than RPG species classes.

traits.name: Metabolic Biology
traits.description: The relevant population is biological and depends on metabolism, biochemical homeostasis, nutrition, and biological health systems.
traits.research_effect: Enables generic biological medicine, life-support, agriculture/food-system, biotechnology, and other metabolic-organism research where applicable.

traits.name: Gravity-Sensitive Biology
traits.description: Long-term health or development changes materially with sustained acceleration/gravity environment.
traits.research_effect: Allows high/low-gravity health and adaptation branches to emerge when real gravity mismatch exists.

traits.name: Heritable Genetic System
traits.description: Biological traits are encoded in a heritable information system that can eventually be deliberately modified with sufficient understanding. The information chemistry need not be terrestrial DNA unless the species specifically uses it.
traits.research_effect: Enables heritable biological engineering and long-term directed adaptation.

traits.name: Metabolic Suppression Physiology
traits.description: The species' physiology can plausibly tolerate a deliberately induced low-metabolism state after adequate medical development. This can be innate or become possible after precursor biological engineering.
traits.research_effect: Makes induced torpor a viable implementation of long-duration habitation.

traits.name: Carbon-Centered Biochemistry
traits.description: The population's core molecular complexity is primarily carbon-centered. This does not specify solvent, atmosphere, temperature regime, or terrestrial compatibility.
traits.research_effect: Enables carbon-specific biochemical solution families where substrate chemistry matters.

traits.name: Water-Solvent Biology
traits.description: Liquid water is the dominant biological solvent over the population's normal active range.
traits.research_effect: Enables water-specific biochemical, medical, ecological, and habitat implementations where solvent chemistry is material.

traits.name: Ammonia-Rich Solvent Biology
traits.description: The population's active biochemistry uses ammonia-rich solvent chemistry substantially enough that water-optimized biological systems are not automatically compatible.
traits.research_effect: Enables ammonia-solvent metabolism, habitat, recycling, nutrient, and bioindustrial branches.

traits.name: Hydrocarbon-Solvent Biology
traits.description: The population relies on liquid hydrocarbon-rich solvents or membranes under cold conditions rather than ordinary water-based cellular chemistry.
traits.research_effect: Enables cryogenic hydrocarbon metabolism, habitat, ecology, and manufacturing branches.

traits.name: Silicon-Centered Biochemistry
traits.description: The population's evolved molecular/structural biochemistry depends substantially on silicon-centered chemistry. This is a speculative rare-life trait and does not imply literal stone organisms or universal high-temperature tolerance.
traits.research_effect: Enables silicon-specific metabolism, repair, structural growth, mineral nutrient, and biofabrication branches.

traits.name: Cryogenic Active Biology
traits.description: Normal biological activity occurs at temperatures where terrestrial liquid-water biology would be severely impaired or frozen.
traits.research_effect: Enables cryogenic metabolism, membrane, ecology, storage, and habitat branches; makes ordinary warm-biological assumptions potentially incompatible.

traits.name: Mineral-Structural Biology
traits.description: Growth and repair rely heavily on controlled mineral/inorganic structural deposition as part of living tissue or analogous biological structure.
traits.research_effect: Enables mineral nutrient control, inorganic tissue repair, mineral biofabrication, and structurally grown habitat/material branches.

traits.name: Liquid-Medium Native Biology
traits.description: The population evolved to live and function primarily within a liquid medium rather than a gas-filled terrestrial surface environment.
traits.research_effect: Can expose fluid-medium habitation, pressure, locomotion, and environmental-interface research when relevant.

traits.name: Machine Cognition Present
traits.description: The civilization contains autonomous machine/synthetic cognition sophisticated enough to exist as persistent agents, institutions, or populations.
traits.research_effect: Enables synthetic-civilization survival, identity, habitat, replication, and machine-population research. A biological civilization can gain this trait through its own technological history.

traits.name: Biological Fabrication Capability
traits.description: The civilization has developed biological manufacturing capable of deliberately growing or assembling engineered structural/industrial material rather than merely modifying organisms for medicine or agriculture.
traits.research_effect: Allows living-material and living-vehicle branches to emerge after enabling biotechnology is mastered, even for a species that did not begin with biological fabrication traditions.
